summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of COPD, chronic diastolic heart failure, obesity hypoventilation syndrome, and obstructive sleep apnea was admitted for dyspnea after noncompliance with oxygen, medications, and diet. She presented with mild respiratory distress and was found to have stable cardiomegaly on chest X-ray and a low BNP, suggesting no acute heart failure exacerbation. Treatment included oxygen, nebulizers, and a prednisone burst for COPD exacerbation, while continuing home diuretics for volume management. A prolonged QTc on EKG led to discontinuation of fluoxetine and trazodone. Her symptoms improved rapidly, and she was discharged to extended care with instructions to complete steroids, use prescribed inhalers and oxygen, monitor weight, and obtain daily EKGs to assess QT interval.
